footer_tag: Read the world, one book at a time.
footer_to_top: Read The Globe, back to the top
landing_hero_sub: Log a novel and your atlas marks two countries: the one the story is set in, and the one its author calls home. Over years of reading, you can see how much of the world you’ve reached.
landing_atlas_desc: Mira’s atlas, an example: a world map that fills in as her 48 books are pinned, ending at 44 of 195 countries, olive where her books are set, rust where her authors come from, striped where both.
landing_band_title: Every book you log goes on the map.
landing_band_sub: One minute per book. The atlas does the rest, from the first pin to the last country on a goal.
landing_panel_log_text: Give a book its title, its author and the author’s country, then the places the story visits. Before you pin it, the form shows which countries it will mark: olive for the setting, rust for the author.
landing_panel_log_alt: Logging a book in the app: The Sympathizer by Viet Thanh Nguyen, author’s country the United States, set in Saigon, Vietnam and Los Angeles. The form shows it will mark the United States and Vietnam.
landing_panel_goals_title: Goals that fill in as you read
landing_panel_goals_text: Pick a region, a set of countries or a theme. A book set there, or by an author from there, moves you along the route until you reach the flag.
landing_panel_goals_alt: Mira’s goals in the app: Around South America, Stories set in the Arctic, The Nordics, Every corner of Europe and Across Africa, each with its map or shelf and its route.
landing_panel_shelf_title: A shelf that remembers every place
landing_panel_shelf_text: Search by title, author, place or country. Bring a reading list in as a CSV, or start with the book on your nightstand.
landing_panel_shelf_alt: Mira’s 2025 shelf in the app: 29 books, each with its cover, author, date, where it is set and where its author is from.
landing_share_sub: Send a card home from wherever your reading has been. Pick one of three:
landing_share_authors_detail: a stamp for every author’s country
landing_share_authors_alt: An example postcard: Mira’s atlas, where her authors come from: a sheet of stamps for 36 of 195 countries, from 48 books on 6 continents.
landing_share_settings_detail: a stamp for every country a story visits
landing_share_settings_alt: An example postcard: Mira’s atlas, where her books are set: a sheet of stamps for 41 of 195 countries, from 48 books on 6 continents.
landing_share_year_detail: one card for each year you’ve logged, ready every December
landing_share_year_alt: An example year postcard: Mira’s 2025, stamps for 27 countries on 5 continents, from 29 books.
landing_share_caption: Mira is an example reader. Every card is saved as a picture, ready for any app.
landing_faq_a1: Yes. Read The Globe is free, and you never need a card.
landing_faq_q2: What if a book is set in several places, or nowhere real?
landing_faq_a2: List every country the story visits. Middle-earth, Earthsea, Narnia and other imagined worlds get a place too, beyond the map.
landing_faq_q3: Do I have to type every book by hand?
landing_faq_a3: No. Import a reading list as a CSV file, with a column each for the title, the author, the author’s country, the places and, if you like, the date; there’s an example file to start from. Your reading list downloads as a CSV too, and a full backup (JSON) keeps your goals as well and restores everything later.
landing_faq_q4: How does a book get its author’s country?
landing_faq_a4: You choose it from the list of 195 countries when you log the book. Familiar names work, so “England” finds the United Kingdom, and for a country that has since split, like Czechoslovakia, you pick which one it is today.
landing_faq_a5: Yes. Send it as a postcard: your atlas as a sheet of stamps or a year in books every December, saved as a picture for any app.
landing_close_title: No streaks, no scores. Just a map that remembers what you’ve read.
